sentences.nl: Marieke is al in het klaslokaal.
sentences.en: Marieke is already in the classroom.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Marieke is already in the classroom.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Al" means "already" and indicates that Marieke is in the classroom earlier than expected.  
• "In het klaslokaal" is a prepositional phrase indicating location. Dutch often uses prepositional phrases to indicate where someone or something is.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Jan is al thuis." (Jan is already at home.)  
  - "De kinderen zijn al buiten aan het spelen." (The children are already playing outside.)  
  - "Zij is al klaar met haar huiswerk." (She is already finished with her homework.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Pieter is al bij de bushalte. (Pieter is already at the bus stop.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No related culture notes.

sentences.nl: Zij is gisteren vroeg naar bed gegaan.
sentences.en: She went to bed early yesterday.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• She is yesterday early to bed gone.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the perfect tense, constructed with "is" as the auxiliary verb and "gegaan" as the past participle. In Dutch, verbs of motion often use "zijn" (to be) rather than "hebben" (to have) as the auxiliary in the perfect tense.  
• Word order: In Dutch, time expressions like "gisteren" (yesterday) typically come before place expressions like "naar bed" (to bed) in a sentence.  
• Example phrases:  
  - Hij is gisteren laat thuisgekomen. (He came home late yesterday.)  
  - Wij zijn vorige week naar Parijs gegaan. (We went to Paris last week.)  
  - Ze is al om acht uur opgestaan. (She got up at eight o'clock already.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Zij is vanochtend vroeg opgestaan. (She got up early this morning.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, it is common to have an early bedtime, especially for children, reflecting a practical approach to balancing work, school, and rest.

sentences.nl: ‘Is het gisteren laat geworden?’ vraagt Marieke.
sentences.en: "Did it get late yesterday?" asks Marieke.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• "Is it yesterday late become?" asks Marieke.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the perfect tense with "geworden" (become), indicating a completed action. "Laat geworden" translates to "became late," a common way to describe staying up late.  
• The word order is typical for Dutch questions, starting with the verb "Is."  
• Example 1: "Is het druk geworden?" (Has it become busy?)  
• Example 2: "Zijn jullie vrienden gebleven?" (Have you remained friends?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Is het weer koud geworden?" (Has the weather become cold again?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, discussing the previous night's events or whether it became "laat" (late) is a common way to start conversations, particularly after social gatherings or parties.

sentences.nl: Ik ben tot half elf gebleven.
sentences.en: I stayed until half past ten.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I am until half ten stayed.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik ben gebleven" uses the present perfect tense, formed with the auxiliary verb "ben" (am) and the past participle "gebleven" (stayed). In Dutch, some verbs use "zijn" (to be) as the auxiliary in the perfect tense, typically verbs of motion or change of state.  
• "Tot half elf" means "until half past ten." In Dutch, "half elf" literally means 10:30, as they count the half-hour towards the next hour.  
• Example: "Ik ben tot half acht gebleven." (I stayed until half past seven.)  
• Example: "Hij is tot kwart over negen gebleven." (He stayed until quarter past nine.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ze is tot half vijf gebleven. (She stayed until half past four.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands and Belgium, the way time is expressed can be confusing for English speakers. "Half elf" means 10:30, not 11:30. It counts the half hour towards the upcoming hour, which is a common practice in many European countries.

sentences.nl: En ik ben om elf uur naar bed gegaan,, nadat we alles hebben schoongemaakt.
sentences.en: And I went to bed at eleven o'clock, after we cleaned everything up.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And I am at eleven o'clock to bed gone, after we everything have cleaned.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the perfect tense ("ben... gegaan" and "hebben... schoongemaakt") which is common for past actions.  
• "Om elf uur" specifies the time, literally "at eleven o'clock."  
• "Nadat" is a conjunction meaning "after" and is used to connect clauses.  

Examples:  
- "Ik ben om negen uur naar huis gegaan." (I went home at nine o'clock.)  
- "Nadat hij het boek heeft gelezen, schreef hij een recensie." (After he read the book, he wrote a review.)  
- "Ze hebben alles schoongemaakt voordat de gasten kwamen." (They cleaned everything before the guests arrived.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "We zijn om zes uur vertrokken, nadat we de auto hadden ingeladen." (We left at six o'clock after we loaded the car.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, it's common to have routines or schedules, especially regarding meal times and bedtime. The specific mention of time (elf uur) suggests a habitual or routine action.

sentences.nl: Bart heeft me gezegd, dat mijn groep 8 studenten heeft.
sentences.en: Bart told me that my group has 8 students.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Bart has me told, that my group 8 students has.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses a perfect tense structure "heeft gezegd" (has said/told), where "heeft" is the auxiliary verb and "gezegd" is the past participle.  
• The word "dat" introduces a subordinate clause, which affects word order. In subordinate clauses, the verb comes at the end.  
• "Groep 8" refers to a specific school year in the Dutch education system, equivalent to grade 6 in the U.S.

Examples:  
• "Ze heeft hem verteld, dat hij moet komen." (She told him that he must come.)  
• "Wij hebben gehoord, dat het morgen regent." (We have heard that it will rain tomorrow.)  
• "Hij zei, dat hij geen tijd heeft." (He said that he has no time.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Mark heeft haar gevraagd, of ze vanavond komt." (Mark asked her if she is coming tonight.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, "groep 8" is the final year of primary school, and students typically prepare for their transition to secondary education during this year.

sentences.nl: Ga jij hier Nederlands studeren? — Maar jij bent gisteren niet bij de barbecue geweest? — Nee, ik ben vandaag gekomen.
sentences.en: Are you going to study Dutch here? — But you weren't at the barbecue yesterday? — No, I came today.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Ga jij hier Nederlands studeren? (Go you here Dutch study?)  
• Maar jij bent gisteren niet bij de barbecue geweest? (But you are yesterday not at the barbecue been?)  
• Nee, ik ben vandaag gekomen. (No, I am today come.)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ga jij hier Nederlands studeren?" uses the future tense with "gaan" + infinitive ("studeren"), a common way to express future actions in Dutch.  
• "Gisteren niet bij de barbecue geweest" uses the perfect tense with "geweest," the past participle of "zijn" (to be), combined with "niet" to express negation.  
• "Vandaag gekomen" also uses the perfect tense, with "gekomen" as the past participle of "komen" (to come).

Examples:  
– Ga je morgen naar de bioscoop? (Are you going to the cinema tomorrow?)  
– Ik ben vorige week naar Amsterdam geweest. (I went to Amsterdam last week.)  
– Hij is net thuis gekomen. (He just came home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ga jij morgen met ons mee naar het museum? (Are you going with us to the museum tomorrow?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The use of "barbecue" in the sentence reflects the popularity of barbecues in the Netherlands during the summer months, often as social gatherings with friends or family.

sentences.nl: In elk geval is iedereen naar de les gekomen.
sentences.en: In any case, everyone came to the class.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• In every case is everyone to the lesson come.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The phrase "In elk geval" means "in any case" or "anyway," and is used to indicate that something is true regardless of other factors.  
• The verb "is gekomen" is in the present perfect tense, indicating a completed action with relevance to the present.  
• The prepositional phrase "naar de les" means "to the lesson," with "naar" indicating direction.  

Examples:  
• In elk geval moeten we op tijd vertrekken. (In any case, we must leave on time.)  
• Iedereen is naar het feest gegaan. (Everyone went to the party.)  
• Hij is naar huis gekomen. (He has come home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• In elk geval heeft zij het geprobeerd. (In any case, she tried.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, punctuality and attending classes are highly valued in educational settings, which is reflected in the sentence emphasizing that everyone came to the lesson.

sentences.nl: Gisteravond? — Dat is al een tijdje geleden…, hmmm…
sentences.en: Last night? — That was a while ago..., hmm...
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Last evening? — That is already a while ago…, hmm…

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Gisteravond" is a compound of "gisteren" (yesterday) and "avond" (evening), used to mean "last evening" or "yesterday evening."  
• "Dat is al een tijdje geleden" uses the phrase "al een tijdje," which means "already a while." This is a common way to express that something happened some time ago.  
• The word "geleden" means "ago" and is often used after a time expression to indicate how long ago something happened.

Examples:  
- "Een jaar geleden" (A year ago)  
- "Dat is al een week geleden" (That was already a week ago)  
- "Het is lang geleden" (It’s been a long time)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Vanmorgen? — Dat lijkt al een eeuw geleden… (This morning? — That feels like ages ago…)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, small talk often includes time references like "gisteravond" or "een tijdje geleden" to set the context for a story or to reminisce about past events. This can be a way to connect with others through shared experiences or memories.

sentences.nl: Ik zal eerst wat over mezelf vertellen.
sentences.en: I will first tell you something about myself.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I will first something about myself tell.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the future tense with "zal" (will) followed by an infinitive verb "vertellen" (to tell).  
• "Eerst" means "first," indicating order.  
• "Wat" is used here to mean "something" or "a bit."  
• "Over mezelf" translates to "about myself," where "over" is a preposition and "mezelf" is a reflexive pronoun.

• Examples:  
  - "Ik zal morgen komen." (I will come tomorrow.)  
  - "Hij moet eerst iets eten." (He must eat something first.)  
  - "Ze vertelt over haar reis." (She talks about her trip.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Morgen zal ik wat meer informatie geven. (Tomorrow I will give some more information.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, introducing oneself with a brief personal story or background, as indicated by "wat over mezelf vertellen," is common in both informal and formal settings, such as meetings or social gatherings.

sentences.nl: Daarna ben ik naar de lerarenopleiding NT2 gegaan.
sentences.en: Afterwards, I went to the NT2 teacher training program.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Thereafter am I to the teacher training NT2 gone.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Daarna" is an adverb meaning "thereafter" or "after that," often used to sequence events.  
• "Ben gegaan" is the present perfect tense of "gaan" (to go), with "ben" as the auxiliary verb because "gaan" is an intransitive verb indicating a change of location.  
• "Naar" is a preposition meaning "to," indicating direction.  
• "De lerarenopleiding NT2" refers to the teacher training program for Dutch as a Second Language.

• Examples:  
  - Daarna heb ik koffie gedronken. (After that, I drank coffee.)  
  - Ik ben naar de supermarkt gegaan. (I went to the supermarket.)  
  - Hij is naar huis gegaan na het werk. (He went home after work.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Daarna ben ik naar de supermarkt gegaan. (After that, I went to the supermarket.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, NT2 refers to "Nederlands als tweede taal" (Dutch as a Second Language), which is a common program for non-native speakers who wish to learn Dutch for integration or professional purposes.

• The sentence uses the present perfect tense, indicated by "heb" (have) and the past participle "gehaald" (obtained).  
• "Mijn diploma" (my diploma) is the direct object, following the auxiliary verb "heb".  
• Word order: The auxiliary verb comes second, followed by the subject, direct object, and the past participle at the end.  
• Extensions:  
  - Ik heb mijn huiswerk gedaan. (I have done my homework.)  
  - Zij heeft een boek gelezen. (She has read a book.)

sentences.nl: En sindsdien werk ik als docent in Rotterdam.
sentences.en: And since then I have been working as a teacher in Rotterdam.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And since then work I as teacher in Rotterdam.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En sindsdien" is a conjunction with an adverb meaning "and since then." It connects events over time.  
• "Werk ik" is an example of inversion; the verb "werk" (work) comes before the subject "ik" (I) because the sentence begins with an adverbial phrase.  
• "Als" is used to indicate a role or capacity, similar to "as" in English.  

• Example 1: "Sindsdien hebben we geen contact meer." (Since then, we have no contact anymore.)  
• Example 2: "Als student heb ik veel geleerd." (As a student, I learned a lot.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En sindsdien woon ik in Amsterdam." (And since then, I live in Amsterdam.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Rotterdam is known for its modern architecture and vibrant cultural scene. It is one of the largest ports in the world.

sentences.nl: ‘Eh… ik ga heel graag naar de kapper!’ lacht Marieke.
sentences.en: "Uh... I really like going to the hairdresser!" laughs Marieke.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• "Eh… I go very gladly to the hairdresser!" laughs Marieke.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik ga heel graag" – This structure uses "graag" to express liking to do something. "Heel" intensifies "graag" to mean "very gladly" or "really like."  
• "naar de kapper" – "Naar" is a preposition meaning "to," and "de kapper" is "the hairdresser."  
• "lacht Marieke" – The verb "lachen" means "to laugh," and the sentence uses inversion, placing the verb before the subject in the reporting clause.

• Extra phrases:  
  - "Ik ga graag naar de bioscoop." (I like to go to the cinema.)  
  - "Zij gaat heel graag wandelen in het park." (She really likes to walk in the park.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Eh… ik ga heel graag naar het strand!" zegt Tom. (Eh… I really like to go to the beach! says Tom.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, visiting the hairdresser ("kapper") is a common and regular social activity, often associated with personal care and relaxation.

## 1. Literal Translation  
• "Wanneer ben je jarig?" vraagt Pablo.  
  "When are you birthday?" asks Pablo.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Wanneer" is an interrogative pronoun meaning "when," used to ask about time.  
• "Ben je jarig" literally translates to "are you birthday," a common way to ask for someone's birth date in Dutch. "Jarig" is an adjective meaning "having a birthday."  
• Verb placement: In a question, the verb "ben" (are) precedes the subject "je" (you), following the structure of Dutch question formation.

• Examples:  
  - "Wanneer kom je thuis?" (When are you coming home?)  
  - "Wanneer begint de film?" (When does the movie start?)  
  - "Ben je morgen vrij?" (Are you free tomorrow?)

sentences.nl: Soliman en Xing kijken naar elkaar…, shsht…
sentences.en: Soliman and Xing look at each other..., shh...
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Soliman and Xing look at each other..., shh...

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "kijken naar elkaar" means "look at each other." The verb "kijken" (to look) is used with the preposition "naar" (at) to indicate the direction of the gaze. "Elkaar" means "each other" and is used when the action is reciprocal.  
• The ellipsis "..." suggests a pause or continuation, and "shsht" is an onomatopoeic representation of a shushing sound.  
• Example phrases:  
  - "Ze praten met elkaar." (They talk with each other.)  
  - "Wij helpen elkaar." (We help each other.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Anna en Mark lachen naar elkaar en fluisteren zachtjes. (Anna and Mark smile at each other and whisper softly.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, making a "shh" sound is a common way to ask for quiet, much like in many other cultures. It's often used in informal settings to gently remind others to lower their volume.

sentences.nl: Heb je de regels van het perfectum goed geleerd? — Ken je ‘t Kofschip? — Dat is heel belangrijk!
sentences.en: Have you learned the rules of the perfect tense well? — Do you know 't Kofschip? — That is very important!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Have you the rules of the perfectum well learned? — Do you know 't Kofschip? — That is very important!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Heb je... geleerd?" is a perfect tense question structure in Dutch, where "heb" is the auxiliary verb and "geleerd" is the past participle.  
• "Ken je 't Kofschip?" uses "ken" (know) in the present tense, with "'t Kofschip" being a mnemonic device for Dutch grammar.  
• "Dat is heel belangrijk" uses "dat" as a demonstrative pronoun and "heel" as an intensifier for "belangrijk" (important).

• Extra Sentences:  
  - "Heb je het boek gelezen?" (Have you read the book?)  
  - "Ken je de weg naar het station?" (Do you know the way to the station?)  
  - "Dat is heel interessant." (That is very interesting.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Heb je de basisprincipes van de grammatica goed begrepen? (Have you understood the basic principles of grammar well?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "'t Kofschip" is a mnemonic used by Dutch speakers to remember which verbs take "ge- + stem + -t" in the past participle. The letters in "’t Kofschip" represent the endings of verbs that use this rule.
